title: OrthographyProfile
description: Declarative description of how a writing system behaves: normalization, matching, segmentation, annotation layers, input aids and layout (gameplan §6.3). Adding a script means adding one of these plus fixtures, not editing the grader.
$comment: v0 (Phase 0). Shapes follow the three examples in gameplan §6.3. Step and policy vocabularies are closed enums on purpose: a new value needs an engine implementation (Phase 1) and conformance vectors before a profile may use it.

exemplars.description: CLDR locale whose main/auxiliary/punctuation/numbers exemplars drive the script audit (§7.5). Both CLDR (yue_Hant) and BCP 47 (yue-Hant) separators are accepted in v0.

exemplarsExtra.description: Characters the orthography uses that its CLDR exemplars lack, such as the Cantonese colloquial characters 佢 哋 嘅 咗 missing from cldr:yue_Hant (CLDR 49). The script audit treats them as main exemplars, and punctuation among them (the Hebrew sof pasuq ׃, missing from cldr:he) as exemplar punctuation. Each entry is a gap to report upstream to CLDR, not a licence to widen the audit.

letters.description: The alphabet as the orthography defines it, including multigraph letters (sh, ch, ng, oʻ). Typo distance and letter-level exercises use it, longest match first.

normalize.description: Applied identically to learner answers and accept sets, in order.

correspondences.description: What this orthography writes of the sound, and what it loses (ADR 0148): the lossy correspondences only. A letter no correspondence names is written as itself and says itself, so an orthography that loses nothing states []. Read by @nabu/core (`project`): grading, spelling-choice cards and the compiler's leftovers (docs/migration-design.md, stages 5 and 6). It replaced `soundAlike` (ADR 0142).

Policy.title: Policy
Policy.description: What the grader does when an answer differs from the accept set only in this respect.

UnicodeSetPattern.title: UnicodeSetPattern
UnicodeSetPattern.description: A UnicodeSet in UTS #35 syntax, e.g. [\u064B-\u0652\u0670].

content.description: Compile-time analyzer that segments content (§7.5), or hand-pinned.

runtime.description: Runtime comparison unit. Never word segmentation (§6.5).

NfcStep.title: NfcStep
NfcStep.description: Canonical composition. NFKC is never a step: compatibility folding only happens through named fold steps (§6.4).

MapStep.title: MapStep
MapStep.description: Literal string replacements, longest key first.

NumberingSystem.title: NumberingSystem
NumberingSystem.description: A CLDR numbering-system id (latn, arab, arabext, hanidec…).

PunctuationStep.title: PunctuationStep
PunctuationStep.description: strip removes General_Category P* only. Modifier letters such as U+02BB and U+02BC (gc=Lm) are letters and are never stripped.

DetachStep.title: DetachStep
DetachStep.description: Splits a prefix written onto the next word off from it, so the attached and the separate spellings compare alike (Arabizi elshay = el shay). A word that starts with one of the prefixes, ignoring case and by whole graphemes, and has at least minRest more graphemes, gets a space after the prefix.

SplitStep.title: SplitStep
SplitStep.description: Puts a space after any of the `after` characters when a letter follows it, so joined and spaced spellings compare alike: Jyutping's tone numbers end its syllables, so hok6saang1 = hok6 saang1 (ADR 0126).

after.description: The characters that end a unit, each one code point (Jyutping: 123456).

ToneNumbersStep.title: ToneNumbersStep
ToneNumbersStep.description: Syllables typed with a tone number after them, written with that tone's mark (ADR 0138): Pinyin typed as xue2 compares as xué. A syllable is the run of letters before the number. Its mark goes on the first letter of the first of `first` the syllable has (a, e, ou: hao3 is hǎo, dou1 is dōu), else on its last letter of `vowels` (liu2 is liú, gui4 is guì); letters compare ignoring case. A number whose mark is empty (the neutral tone) is dropped; a number with no mark, or a syllable with nowhere to put it, is left as it is.

marks.description: Each tone number and the combining mark it stands for (\u0301 for 2), or an empty string where the tone has none.

vowels.description: The letters that may carry a tone's mark, each a grapheme: aeiouü.

first.description: Where the mark goes before the last vowel: the first of these the syllable has, its first letter (a, e, ou).

LogographsStep.title: LogographsStep
LogographsStep.description: Words typed in a script that spells them, written as this orthography's logographs (ADR 0086): a learner can type sitelen pona as sitelen Lasina, toki for U+F196C. Each whole word (a run of letters and marks) that is a key, ignoring case, becomes its value. With `cartouche`, a name written inside one reads as the letters its logographs begin with (open, sona, olin, nasin, jan, a, close is sonja), the marks dropped, so a name typed in Latin letters compares alike. Names are read before words, so a name that spells a word (kili) becomes that word's logograph on both sides.

words.description: Each word, as it is typed, and the logograph that writes it.

cartouche.description: The marks that open and close a name written with the logographs' first letters.

optional.description: Marks of the set a learner supplying a word's vowel marks (the vocalize exercise, ADR 0054) may write or leave out: sukun, where the course's conventions differ.

optionalBefore.description: Marks a learner supplying a word's vowel marks (ADR 0054 as amended) may write or leave out on a letter, where the letter after it is one of `letters`: the fatha before the alif that writes its long a (مَرْحَبا and مَرْحَبَا are the same word), the kasra before a bare ya that writes its long i (فيلِم and فِيلِم). The same mark elsewhere counts as the others do.

letters.description: The letters before which they may be written or not: whole letters, as NFC writes them (a plain alif, never one carrying a hamza).

bare.description: Only where that letter, in the expected word, carries no mark of the set: a ya or waw that writes a long vowel. One with a mark of its own (مِيِّة, هُوّ) is a consonant, and the vowel before it counts.

unless.description: Marks of the set on the letter itself, in the expected word, that keep the marks counting: a sukun says the letter after begins a syllable, so it is a consonant (فاضْيين: fāḍyīn, never fāḍiyīn).

optionalOn.description: Marks a learner supplying a word's vowel marks (ADR 0054 as amended) may write or leave out on one of `letters` itself, whose letter already says them: the kasra under an alif with a hamza below (إِمّ and إمّ: the hamza below says i). The same mark on any other letter counts.

letters.description: The letters that already say them: whole letters, as NFC writes them.

required.description: Marks of the set an answer must write as the expected word does (ADR 0134): one left out, added, changed or moved is never folded away by the policy and never a typo, and the word is wrong (WRONG_WORD where it spells another word of the course, with `wordNote`). Chaghatay's transliteration: the vowel marks (ä ö ü ā ī ū ē à), which say what the Arabic script leaves out. Its consonant marks keep the policy, but for `requiredLetters`.

requiredNote.description: The note for an answer whose only difference is in its `required` marks.

requiredLetters.description: Letters written with a mark of the set, whose mark an answer must write as the expected word does (ADR 0134 as amended by ADR 0148): such a letter written without its mark, its bare letter written with it, or another mark of the set in its place is never folded away by the policy and never a typo, and the word is wrong, as with `required`. The same mark on any other letter keeps the policy, and the whole letter traded for another, left out or added is a slip like any other letter's (the typo model and the contrast sets judge it). Chaghatay's transliteration: š, ž, ḫ and ǧ, which without their mark are s, z, h and g, other sounds and other Arabic letters. (ṣ, ḥ, ṭ and the rest sound as their plain letter does, and č has no plain letter to be taken for: those stay with the policy.)

requiredLettersNote.description: The note for an answer whose only difference is in the marks of its `requiredLetters`. Where `required` marks differ too, `requiredNote` is given.

distinguishes.description: Marks that tell words apart (ADR 0076): the Spanish tilde in está/esta, sí/si, habló/hablo. An answer whose marks differ from the expected word's and so spell another word of the course (the grader's lexicon) is WRONG_WORD, with `wordNote`; otherwise the policy applies.

wordNote.description: The note for an answer whose marks spell another word (with `distinguishes`).

spelledIn.description: Orthographies that write out the vowels these marks leave unwritten (ADR 0095): Arabizi for Lebanese Arabic. Where a course has one of them, a vocalize card also accepts the word as that orthography writes it.

minLength.description: Tokens shorter than this many units get no typo tolerance (default 3).

contrasts.description: Endings, or whole words, that carry meaning, in sets: person endings, possessive endings, case endings, pronouns. A slip that turns one member of a set into another at the end of a word, the rest unchanged, is WRONG_WORD, not a typo: talabasan for talabaman, kitobing for kitobim (erratum 46). Members match after case folding, the profile's equivalences and its marks, as units are compared, so a hamza-less spelling still counts. A member may list several spellings of one meaning (the dative ga, ka, qa): trading those stays a typo.

equivalences.description: Folds applied to both the answer and the accept set only for comparison, each with its own policy, e.g. Arabic hamza seats (accept-with-note) or Arabizi ch/sh (accept). The first equivalence that makes two units equal decides the policy; normalization steps, by contrast, fold silently.

joins.description: Words the orthography writes onto the word after them or apart, in forms no norm picks among (Arabizi's article: el shay, elshay, l shay, lshay, esh shay). Grading compares word by word; these let one or two typed words stand for the joining word and the word after it, only where the accepted answer has the joining word there.

Join.title: Join
Join.description: A joining word (`joins`). Where an accepted answer has one of its forms followed by a word W (written apart, or split off by a `detach` step), or a word that begins with one of its assimilated forms whose letter is written twice (essalame), an answer that writes any of its forms followed by a spelling that compares as W (the profile's equivalences, free correspondences or a slip; W's other-lexeme and other-form guards hold), as one word or two, is that answer: CORRECT_VARIANT with `note` where the forms differ, nothing more where only the space does. An answer's word is split only there, and never where it is a word the course writes of another lexeme. No form is empty: the word left out stays left out.

assimilates.description: Its forms before a word that begins with a letter of `before` (Arabizi's sun letters), beside `forms`: in each, {next} (only at its end) is that letter written again (e{next}: essalame, es salame).

before.description: The letters; {sh} for one written with two.

minRest.description: The word after it has at least this many graphemes (default 3), so el li, which a detach step makes of elli, is no joining word and word.

notBefore.description: Never before a word the course stands only as one of these parts of speech (the grader's `forms`): el bos, which a detach step makes of elbos (I wear), is no article and noun.

note.description: The note for a form other than the accepted answer's (default spelling-variant).

NoteId.title: NoteId
NoteId.description: Key of a feedback note in the MF2 catalogs (feedback.note.<id>).

lang.description: The language tag of the layer's own text (ADR 0071), so it is announced and shaped as what it is: Jyutping is yue-Latn-jyutping, Pinyin zh-Latn-pinyin, Baxter's Middle Chinese ltc-Latn-x-baxter. Without it the annotation takes the base text's tag.

spell.description: How the layer's text is written from a lexical form (a vocalization layer: the marked text the voices read). Its `rules` run over the form as the profile's own do.

markBuilder.description: A vocalize card may also ask the word's vowel marks put on its letters, the letters given and the marks on buttons (`vocalize-build`, ADR 0137), once a choice card has shown them. For an abjad whose marks no phone keyboard has.

extraKeys.description: Characters for the special-character bar, in addition to the auxiliary exemplars (§6.7).

vertical.description: Which vertical writing mode the orthography supports, if any (§11.4).

verticalPolicy.description: toggle: vertical is a user option (CJK). always: the orthography is only ever set vertically (traditional Mongolian). Defaults to toggle.

verticalScope.description: Surfaces that may switch to vertical. App chrome never does.

scale.description: How much larger than the text around it the orthography's text is set (1: the same). Han characters at the size of the Latin around them are hard to read: Classical Chinese is 1.25 (ADR 0071). The learner's text size preference scales both.

Speech.title: SpeechSetup
Speech.description: How speech in the orthography is heard (gameplan §10.4, ADR 0116): what the speech service scores a learner on, the recognizer that hears it (learners, and the round trip of the course's clips) and where expected phones come from (tier 2, and forced alignment of clips). A profile without it is scored on nothing; its recognizer and phones take their defaults.

tiers.description: What the speech service scores (REVIEW: per-language choices, to revisit with recorded learners). 1: the words, where the recognizer writes this orthography; the API grades its transcript with the sentence's accept set. 2: the phones, where the expected phones can be trusted. Empty: nothing.

Recognizer.title: Recognizer
Recognizer.description: Who hears the orthography: Whisper, in a language, or a Whisper fine-tune for a language Whisper's own does not write (Cantonese, which it writes as Mandarin: ADR 0094).

language.description: The language Whisper hears it as. Default: the profile's language, or, where Whisper has none for it, the macrolanguage that encompasses it (CLDR's data: apc is heard as ar).

FineTunedRecognizer.title: FineTunedRecognizer
FineTunedRecognizer.description: A Whisper fine-tune that hears the language instead of Whisper's own.

model.description: Its Hugging Face repo and pinned revision: "alvanlii/whisper-small-cantonese@b03a4e5d482f06858ce10ebbabebabec9f447a0d".

token.description: The Whisper language token it was trained with ("zh").

SpeechPhones.title: SpeechPhones
SpeechPhones.description: Where expected phones come from: the reading each word pins in `reading`, where that scheme gives phones (Jyutping), else eSpeak NG's phonemes of the spelling in `voice`.

voice.description: The eSpeak NG voice that reads the spelling. Default: the profile's language, or, where eSpeak NG has no voice for it, the macrolanguage that encompasses it (apc is read as ar).

ScriptTrack.title: ScriptTrack
ScriptTrack.description: What an alphabet track teaching this orthography asks its letters and words as (ADR 0088, 0124, 0133): their reading in `reading`, written in that scheme's `latin` for a learner who cannot read the script yet. A word's is its lexeme's pinned reading (ADR 0117), the one its word card and clip take, through the scheme's `latin` plug-in where the scheme's own text is not Latin (Attic: χώρᾱ is chōrā); a letter, which has no reading, is the plug-in's rendering of the letter, or where the scheme has none (an abjad's letter stands for several sounds), its grapheme KC's own form in the scheme's `latin` orthography.

reading.description: The reading scheme the track asks (attic, schluessel): one the orthography's words pin, with a `latin` orthography.

map.description: Literal replacements, longest key first, applied to both sides.

TableRef.title: TableRef
TableRef.description: Id of a data table in profiles/tables/<id>.json (schemas/data-table.schema.json).

Contrast.title: Contrast
Contrast.description: A set of endings, prefixes (or whole words) one letter or two apart that mean different things.

members.description: The members, each a meaning. An empty spelling is the word with no such affix: the bare Lebanese imperfect (shteghel) beside b-shteghel, a masculine adjective beside its feminine.

at.description: Where the members stand: at the end of the word (endings, stacking like suffixes) or at its start (prefixes: Lebanese b-, bt-, mn- on verbs). Default end.

after.description: For prefixes: what may come before the member, a proclitic written onto the word (Arabic و 'and': وبشتغل).

inflected.description: Only on words the course inflects: a word the grader is told carries a form (GradeOptions.inflected: the spellings of a lexeme some token writes outside its part of speech's bare cell). A noun's first letter is a typo; a verb's prefix is not.

forms.description: Only on words that a token of the course writes in one of these forms (GradeOptions.forms: the forms of the tokens a word spells). Narrower than inflected, for a course whose nouns have forms too: Biblical Hebrew's person prefixes are a verb's, never a noun's first letter, and its perfect endings a perfect's, never an infinitive's (ADR 0084).

note.description: The feedback note shown with the verdict (MF2 message feedback.note.<note>).

Correspondence.title: Correspondence
Correspondence.description: One correspondence between a sound and the ways an orthography writes it (ADR 0148: the projections are rules, and the profile states them). In a profile it is read forwards: at each place of a spelling the longest `written` whose `when` holds wins, the earlier correspondence on a tie (state a narrower context before a wider one). In a reading scheme with `of` it relates a piece of the reading to the spelling of that orthography. Whatever the stated correspondences do not give is per lexeme: a leftover to learn, or a pinned spelling to review. A correspondence may not say nothing and be written only as nothing (`says: ""` with `written: [""]`): @nabu/core refuses to compile it.

says.description: A sound in the profile's own notation, or a piece of the reading in the scheme's: only ever compared for equality. An empty string: written and not said (Spanish h).

written.description: The ways it is written. An empty string: not written (said and not written), meaningful only in a scheme's relation; a profile's reading skips it.

kind.description: fixed: the norm picks one spelling for each lexeme, so where there are several, which one is a leftover (fa: sin, sad or se). free: no norm picks one, so each is right and none is a leftover (Arabizi: e or i).

rare.description: Ways the sound is also written that the norm keeps for a few words or never uses where `written` stands (Spanish k for the sound of c and qu; Uzbek Cyrillic йа for я). They are read as the same sound, so one typed for the usual spelling is an orthographic miss; but none is offered in place of a usual spelling, and a word written the usual way has no leftover from them. A word the norm does write with one (kilo) has its leftover: its usual spellings are what a card offers. A profile's statement only.

loses.description: The other pieces written the same way, which reading back cannot tell from `says`: a set a reading card may trade within (Pinyin's ā among á, ǎ, à). Used by schemes; a profile's reading ignores it.

note.description: The feedback note for a spelling that differs only by this.

Spell.title: Spell
Spell.description: How this orthography writes a lexical form (docs/rules-design.md, section 3): the other direction of its sound statement. `rules` rewrite the form, in order, into the spelling; a rule's `alternatives` are the free spellings, each named by the variation it is. Read by @nabu/core (`compileSpeller`, `spell`) in the compiler only: a bundle never carries it. Patterns are written in the language's notation (its `order` of marks); {name} is a set of the notation's `sets` or of this statement's.

from.description: What is spelled: a lexeme's lexical form, in its language's notation.

boundaries.description: true: a realised form's boundaries (+) stay for the rules to name, and are dropped after them: an orthography that writes where a suffix joins (chg's half-space). Without it they are dropped first.

decompose.description: true: the rules read the form decomposed (NFD), each letter's marks apart from it and in the notation's `order`, so a rule can find a mark that NFC composes into its letter (Greek ά: α and an acute); the spelling is NFC again.

sets.description: Named sets of this statement's own, beside the notation's.

rules.description: None where the orthography writes the form as it is (its boundaries dropped).

SpellRule.title: SpellRule
SpellRule.description: One rewrite, applied at every place `find` matches with its context holding, left to right and not overlapping, before the next rule runs. A pattern is letters and marks as themselves, {name} (a named set: one of its members), [...] (a UnicodeSet), ( | ) to group and choose, ? and * after a piece, ^ and $ for a word's start and end, and a backslash before a sign meant as itself. `to` replaces the match ({name} in it is what the find's {name} of the same rank matched); `map`, given instead of `to`, replaces it by its entry. A word is a run of the form between spaces.

after.description: What must stand right before the match.

before.description: What must stand right after the match.

at.description: start: `after` (or the match) begins a word; end: `before` (or the match) ends one.

alternatives.description: Free spellings: at each place the rule applies, one of these may stand in place of `to`. Each is named by its variation, so what a variation would accept can be counted (the owner's question 6, docs/rules-design.md).

SpellAlternative.title: SpellAlternative
SpellAlternative.description: A free spelling of what a rule writes: `to` in place of the rule's, the variation named by `id`.

CorrespondenceContext.title: CorrespondenceContext
CorrespondenceContext.description: Where a correspondence holds, tested on the written side. Every key given must hold.

at.description: At the start or the end of the word.

before.description: The letter right after it is one of these (never at the word's end).

after.description: The letter right before it is one of these (never at the word's start).

SoundSource.title: SoundSource
SoundSource.description: Where a word's sound comes from, for the sound question of grading and the spelling cards (ADR 0148). spelling: what the profile's correspondences read off its spelling. reading: its token's pinned reading in `scheme`, related to the spelling by that scheme's statement. Absent: the sound question is never asked for this orthography.

ignores.description: Marks the sound reading leaves aside (fa's vowel marks: the unmarked spelling is the usual one).

scheme.description: The scheme whose pinned readings are the sound. Marks of a spelling that the relation passes over are the scheme's `ignores`.

Stress.title: Stress
Stress.description: Where a mark writes stress and a rule places it otherwise (es): the stress is made explicit before a spelling is compared, so esta and está say different things and háblo says hablo. Only meaningful with `sound: {from: spelling}`.

mark.description: The combining mark that writes stress (U+0301).

vowels.description: The `says` values that are syllable nuclei.

weak.description: The vowels that join a neighbouring vowel in one syllable unless they carry the mark (i, u).

default.description: Where an unmarked word of two syllables or more is stressed: the first rule whose `when` holds.

ends.description: The written word's last letter is one of these.

note.description: The feedback note for a spelling that differs by the stress mark.

FormCondition.title: FormCondition
FormCondition.description: A form a token may stand in: its base lexeme's part of speech (any, where none is given) and feature values it has there, chosen on the token or its lexeme's own. Every feature named must have one of the values given (several, separated by commas: any of them). The perfect of a Hebrew verb: {feats: {Aspect: Perf, VerbForm: Fin}}; a feminine noun or adjective: {pos: [NOUN, ADJ], feats: {Gender: Fem}}.
